headerBody: Morocco: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented against the DGSN and Brigade Touristique (tourist police), ONMT tourism advisories, Morocco World News reporting, and firsthand traveler accounts. It maps the exact scripts on Djemaa el-Fna, in the Fez tanneries, and out in the Erg Chebbi dunes — the red flags that give each one away, and the Darija phrases that shut them down.
quadHead: Four ways Morocco catches tourists off guard.

quad.title: The Henna Tattoo Ambush
quad.tl: A woman on Djemaa el-Fna grabs your wrist with 'for luck, no money,' paints a design before you can pull away, then two male relatives appear demanding 200–300 MAD.

quad.title: The Camel-Trek Upcharge
quad.tl: A handler quotes 200 MAD for a sunset trek, rides 90 minutes 'to make it worth it,' then demands an extra 200 MAD plus 100 MAD in photo fees with the camels wedged between dunes.

quad.title: The Fake Trilobite Fossil
quad.tl: A roadside seller offers a stunning trilobite for 300 MAD — about 90% sold to tourists are cement, painted and acid-aged; real specimens cost 5–10x more from certified Erfoud dealers.

quad.title: The Hash-Tout Police Setup
quad.tl: A young man sells you hash in the medina; minutes later a 'police officer' steps out demanding 2,000–5,000 MAD to avoid arrest — the seller and the officer split the take.

body: Morocco: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented — not recycled — against DGSN and Brigade Touristique (tourist police) guidance, ONMT tourism advisories, Morocco World News reporting, and firsthand traveler accounts.

61 specific scams across Marrakech, Fez, Chefchaouen, Merzouga, Tangier and five more destinations. The exact scripts, the red flags that give them away, and the Darija phrases that shut them down — written in romanized script you can read straight off your phone.

Scams evolve, so the book is re-researched and updated every year — when a new edition ships, it appears in your Kindle library. Built for the traveler who wants to move through Morocco relaxed, not braced.
